chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan and Ali ibn Hakam together, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, who said:

The ordinances (alwah) came to us from Abul Hasan (peace be upon him) while he was in prison: My testament to the eldest of my sons is that he should do such-and-such. As for so-and-so, do not give him anything until you meet me or God decrees death for me.

key_terms.أَلْوَاحٌ: Plural of lawh, meaning tablets, boards, or written ordinances/documents.
key_terms.فُلَانٌ: So-and-so (a placeholder name used for a specific individual).

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Kadhim decree regarding the inheritance and leadership of his sons while in prison?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* provides crucial evidence for the Imamate of Imam Ali al-Rida (peace be upon him) by documenting a formal, written designation (khitba) from his father, Imam Musa al-Kadhim, while the latter was imprisoned. The text highlights the distinction between the primary successor and other sons, illustrating the precise mechanism of hereditary succession (nas) within the Ahl al-Bayt during the Abbasid era. It underscores the continuity of authority and the specific theological status of the eldest son as the designated heir in this particular lineage branch.
